stepsTitle: How it works: convert Excel to CSV

steps.title: Drop your Excel file
steps.text: Drop an .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .ods file on this page or choose it. It is read in your browser and never uploaded.

steps.title: It opens as a CSV
steps.text: The first sheet is converted at once and opens in the CSV viewer, with commas between the columns and Arabic text kept intact.

steps.title: Check and edit it
steps.text: Search, sort, filter and edit the rows in the CSV viewer, so the CSV holds exactly what you need.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Download saves the CSV. For a semicolon, tab or pipe instead of a comma, choose Download options in the More menu.

handlesTitle: What the Excel to CSV converter handles
handles: Values: each cell as Excel shows it, so dates, percentages and currencies keep their format, and formulas give their saved result.
Sheets: the first sheet; for another, open the workbook in the Excel viewer, pick the sheet and use Convert.
Encoding: UTF-8, with the byte order mark Excel needs for Arabic and other non-Latin text whenever the sheet has any.
Delimiters: a comma, or a semicolon, tab or pipe from the CSV viewer's Download options.
limits: CSV holds values only: formulas, formatting, charts and images are not kept.
Each sheet becomes its own CSV file.
faqTitle: Excel to CSV: questions and answers

faq.question: How do I convert an Excel file with several sheets to CSV?
faq.answer: This page converts the first sheet. For another sheet, open the workbook in the Excel viewer, click the sheet's tab, then click Convert at the top and choose Convert to CSV: the sheet on screen opens as a CSV.

faq.question: Why does Arabic text look broken when I open the CSV in Excel?
faq.answer: Excel reads a UTF-8 file without a byte order mark as an older Windows encoding. The CSV made here gets that mark whenever the sheet has Arabic or other non-Latin text, so Excel shows it correctly.

link.text: Fix broken Arabic in a CSV

faq.question: Can I use a semicolon instead of a comma?
faq.answer: Yes. The CSV opens in the CSV viewer: choose Download options in the More menu and pick a semicolon, tab or pipe. A semicolon suits Excel in regions that write decimals with a comma, where a comma-separated file lands in one column.

faq.question: Are formulas kept in the CSV?
faq.answer: No. CSV holds text only, so each formula is written as the result saved in the workbook. Keep the Excel file if you still need the formulas.

faq.question: Are dates and numbers written the way Excel shows them?
faq.answer: Yes. Each cell is written as the text Excel shows, so a date stays 05/01/2026 and a price keeps its currency sign, instead of becoming the number Excel stores behind it.

faq.question: Is my workbook uploaded to convert it?
faq.answer: No. The workbook is read and converted by your browser on your device; nothing is sent to a server.
